label: The sk-code surface axis is selected by stack markers and .github/ is not one of them: detect_surface_evidence returns exactly SKILLED, OBSIDIAN, WEBFLOW or UNKNOWN, the four detection branches never test .github/, and the generic-Node guard drops everything else to UNKNOWN, so a review of .github/workflows/*.yml gets baseline security/correctness only and prints 'Surface evidence used: UNKNOWN'. An sk-code-ci standards packet therefore cannot be reached by diff path today; reaching it needs either a fifth surface value in the shared contract or a diff-path conditional inside the review packet.

The review packet states that its detect_surface_evidence restates the shared contract and keeps no rules of its own, so it changes only when the contract does; a CI surface is therefore one contract edit plus one packet restatement, and the two cannot drift by policy. It is also the only coupling path that touches every sk-code consumer at once (quality, review, three surfaces), which is why it belongs last.

The surface set is a closed enumerated list (extensions.surface-axis.surfaces names the three packets) and the hub fails loudly on a half-declared axis: check 3f fails when the extension is declared with no surface mode, and 5f soft-fails when surface packets exist without the surfaceBundle outcome. Adding sk-code-ci as a surface is four edits and no outcome change: the mode entry, the extension surfaces array, a routerSignals entry, and a tieBreak slot ahead of the native surface.

Check 3k reads a mode's command field through COMMAND_PATTERN, resolves it to .skilled/commands/<dir>/<name>.md, and soft-fails when that command's frontmatter allowed-tools exceed the mode's toolSurface.allowed. No sk-code mode declares command today, so 3k has never compared anything on this hub. Because 3g forces a surface to evidence-base, mutatesWorkspace:false and an allowed set drawn from Read/Bash/Grep/Glob, a scaffolding command cannot declare command: on a read-only surface mode - so the surface mode carries no command field and the doctor route owns the mutation.

The doctor route manifest is the mutation authority: every route declares mutating as read-only | add-only | mutates plus a concrete gate3_location, and route-validate.sh asserts the key set, asset existence, duplicate targets, that the named router exists (B3), target-set parity against the real routers (J1), and a read-only-mutation policy (K1) that fails a read-only route whose own YAML writes. /doctor:ci is therefore a mutates route with a named target file, and its dry-run default is a route-level property rather than a prompt promise.

A new doctor target is a documented four-step act: append the route with three-or-more-word trigger phrases; list the target in the owning command's router and presentation and add its row to /doctor:setup's target list; add its activation entry to both the typescript and python lists in scoring-compatibility.json because a bridge without one stays inactive; then rerun derive-command-bridges.cjs, route-validate.sh and doctor-phrase-reach.cjs. A command that owns one route needs no positional target, each doctor command is a thin router owning a YAML workflow plus a separate presentation asset, and each is mirrored into four runtime command directories.

Inferred: the phase order is forced by the gates. First the sk-code-ci standards packet, which lands without mutating anything outside sk-code (mode entry, extension array, routerSignals, tieBreak, leaf-manifest regeneration, ROUTER.md) and is read-only by contract. Second /doctor:ci, whose scaffolding must read the packet's templates or the route inlines them and creates two sources of truth. Third the review wiring, which edits a shared contract four packets restate and is the only step that can regress detection for the three existing surfaces. Risk/effort: packet low/low, /doctor:ci medium/medium, review wiring low/medium. Falsifier: shipping review wiring with the packet in one change trades a second review cycle for one larger diff.

Inferred: /doctor:ci should split into two routes rather than be one mutating command, because mutating is per-route not per-command - one router file can own a read-only list/report route and a mutates scaffold route, giving the dry-run default a structural home and keeping K1 satisfied for the read-only half. The toggle half is bounded by the earlier finding that repository variables are readable but not writable without an admin token, so its route is at most add-only (printed instruction plus a verification read). Ownership split: standards in the sk-code surface packet, inventory/report/scaffold in the doctor route manifest, and nothing in sk-git except committing a scaffolded file.

direction: Register sk-code-ci as a surface packet that /doctor:ci binds via the mode's command field
reason: 3k would compare the command's frontmatter against the surface's allowed set, and 3g forces a surface to Read/Bash/Grep/Glob with mutatesWorkspace:false, so a scaffolder declaring Write or Edit fails the check it was supposed to pass.

direction: Rely on surface detection to route workflow-YAML diffs to an sk-code-ci packet without touching the shared contract
reason: None of the four detection branches tests .github/; the generic-Node guard returns UNKNOWN, so the packet would never be bundled for the diffs it exists to govern.
